solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suitably clad doctor saying nothing

indicators.note: clad means dressed, so the word for suitably wraps around the doctor like clothing

parts.note: suitably means duly, in the proper way
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor stands silent, though at least they are properly dressed for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' here is the medical degree abbreviation, and 'clad' wraps 'Suitably' around it like clothing rather than describing dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without speech is doing it mutely, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Delivers sweets no longer on the menu

parts.note: drops are small boiled sweets, like pear drops or lemon drops
a dish that has run out in a restaurant is said to be off

explanation.surface: A shop takes certain sweets out of its range, as if a menu had been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a parcel or passenger is to leave it at its destination, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: What martial arts trainer needs for beginners?

definitions.text: What martial arts trainer needs for beginners?

indicators.note: beginners are the starting letters, so the first letter of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: A question about what kit a martial arts coach needs when teaching novices.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the initials of 'martial arts trainer' spell the item a trainer needs so beginners can fall safely.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial arts are practised on a padded floor covering that cushions throws and falls.

clue.text: Descent made by majority at end of rope

indicators.note: the word for majority is placed after the end of the word for rope

parts.note: a line is a rope, especially on a ship
the age of majority is when one legally becomes an adult, so majority can mean age

explanation.surface: A climber makes a descent at the end of a rope, aided by most of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority' tempts as 'most of'; here it is the legal coming of age.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent in the sense of ancestry or family line is a synonym for this word for pedigree.

clue.text: Bureaux and top-rank clubs invested in bottled spirits?

parts.note: A, as in A1 or grade A, means first-class

indicators.note: invested here means put inside, so the clubs letter goes into the spirits

parts.note: genies are the spirits kept in bottles or lamps in folk tales
C is the card-playing abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Bureaux and elite clubs have money tied up in stocks of bottled liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottled spirits' suggests drink, but it means genies. 'invested in' puts C inside GENIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Bureaux are offices providing a service, such as employment or travel agencies.

clue.text: Ultimate sale bargain apparently worthless

definitions.meaning: read literally, an item you get without paying anything is the best bargain of a sale
useless, of no value, said of a lazy person or thing

explanation.surface: A bargain at the sales turns out, apparently, to be quite valueless.
explanation.walkthrough: Read word by word, the answer means 'fine for zero cost', the best a sale can offer; as a phrase it means useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone or something useless and of no value is the everyday sense of this idiom.

clue.text: Increasingly unbalanced cask carried up bank

indicators.note: in a down entry, carried up means the word is written bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer
a tier is a row or bank, as of seats or oars

explanation.surface: A wobbly barrel is hauled up a riverbank, growing ever more unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried up' reverses TUN to NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbalanced in the sense of mentally unhinged is crazy, and the comparative is madder or crazier.

clue.text: Is dieting on crackers its cause?

definitions.text: Is dieting on crackers its cause?

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters of these three words go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether living on crackers is what is upsetting their stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the biscuits being eaten, but it is the anagram signal; the whole clue also defines the answer as the result of a cracker diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia, stomach discomfort after eating, is what a diet of dry biscuits might bring on.

clue.text: Customary small drink drained daily

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
tea is a common drink

indicators.note: drained means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A habitual little drink is finished off every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained' empties daily to DY.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary means regular or habitual, as in a regular, settled routine or a constant partner.

clue.text: Preserve support after biblical queen briefly deposed king

indicators.note: the word for support comes after the queen's name

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Esther is the Jewish queen of Persia in the Old Testament book named after her
to second is to support a motion or proposal

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch is propped up by a biblical queen and some jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims ESTHER to ESTHE. James II was the Stuart king of England deposed in 1688.
explanation.definitionFit: James II lost his throne in the Glorious Revolution of 1688, the classic English monarch removed from power.

clue.text: Sailor included in total recovering from attack?

indicators.note: the sailor's letters are placed inside the phrase for total

parts.note: out-and-out means complete or total, as in an out-and-out liar
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is fully involved in recovery after being mugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attack' is an attack of illness, not a mugging; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting over an illness, like an attack of flu, is up and moving around again.

clue.text: Feminine counterpart of stag party, bride's last

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: the last letter of the word bride is taken

explanation.surface: The female equivalent of a stag party, the hen night, is the bride's final fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stag party' looks like one unit, but 'stag' belongs to the definition and 'party' to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, and its female is the hind or this word for a female deer.

clue.text: Glimpse errand boy's narrow escape?

parts.note: to glimpse is to see briefly
a page is a boy who runs errands, as in a hotel

explanation.surface: An errand boy is spotted making a narrow escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'boy' is a link; the definition is liquid escaping through a narrow gap, a leak.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that oozes out slowly through tiny gaps is a leak through a narrow opening.

clue.text: Legal appointee's administrator leading seminar: not the first time

indicators.note: the administrator's letters lead, coming before the rest

parts.note: exec is short for executive, an administrator

indicators.note: the first occurrence of the letter for time is removed from the word for seminar

parts.note: a tutorial is a small teaching seminar

explanation.surface: A legal official's manager is chairing a seminar, though it is hardly their first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first time' removes the opening T from TUTORIAL, leaving UTORIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An executor is the person appointed to carry out a will, and this adjective means relating to that role.

clue.text: Female with band having an edge

parts.note: ringed means encircled with a band or ring

explanation.surface: A woman with a group of musicians has an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but it is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bordered by a decorative edging of threads or tassels has a trimmed margin.

clue.text: Economic system I represent, perhaps?

parts.note: if the letters of the word for a business venture are set free, or shuffled, they spell these two words

explanation.surface: A political figure claims to embody a particular economic system.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read 'free' as an anagram signal and the answer is an instruction that turns ENTERPRISE into I REPRESENT. 'perhaps' warns it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitalism with little state control is the market-driven economy this phrase names.

clue.text: Mole, tailed, sits atop ditch

indicators.note: tailed means having the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a mole is a harbour breakwater, also called a jetty
something that sits atop another is on it, giving the two short words for that

explanation.surface: A burrowing mole, seen from behind, perches on the edge of a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' is not the animal but a stone pier, a jetty; 'tailed' drops its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to throw it away, as cargo is thrown overboard to lighten a ship.

clue.text: What's cooking? Silly rhetorical question unruly tots ignored

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so these letters are mixed up
unruly means disorderly, so the small children's letters are taken out in any order
ignored means left out, so those letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Someone asks what's for dinner, a silly question the unruly children don't answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of RHETORICAL QUESTION, remove T, O, T, S, and rearrange the rest into the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury egg-and-bacon tart from Lorraine is an example of something being baked in the kitchen.

clue.text: Highly imitative journalism, spiteful type

parts.note: copy is the text of journalism written for publication
a cat is a spiteful or catty person, especially a malicious gossip

explanation.surface: A newspaper's writing is accused of plagiarism by a bitchy critic.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in crimes imitating an earlier one, the word describes slavish mimicry.

clue.text: Extra violin part you might have at La Scala?

definitions.text: you might have at La Scala?

indicators.note: part signals that only some of the letters of the two words are taken, in sequence

explanation.surface: An extra violin part could be heard at Milan's famous opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a musical part but marks the letters hidden across 'Extra violin'. La Scala is Milan's opera house, so the definition is Italian food you might eat there.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffed pasta squares are a classic Italian dish, the sort of food you might eat in Milan.

clue.text: Makes off with socks

definitions.meaning: steals, as a thief grabs an item
hits or punches, as in sweeping blows

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are slang: steals in quick snatches, and hits with wild, sweeping strikes.

clue.text: Circlet with tiny casing that delights me

indicators.note: casing means enclosing, so the word for tiny wraps around the circlet

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny
a hoop is a small circular band

explanation.surface: A tiny ring in its little case makes someone very happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiny' is Scottish wee, which does the casing; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation of joy is what someone shouts when something pleases them.

clue.text: Person with little boats oddly banned by port

parts.note: a haven is a harbour or port

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word are banned, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A port forbids certain small boats from mooring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly banned' removes B, A and S from boats, leaving OT, which comes by HAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The poor are contrasted with the rich as those lacking possessions, the opposite of the haves.

clue.text: Letter from the Balkans, far from neutral

definitions.meaning: a Greek letter, since Greece is a Balkan country
pH 1, written as the letters pH and the numeral one, is strongly acidic, far from the neutral reading of 7

explanation.surface: A letter arrives from a Balkan country that is anything but neutral in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading needs chemistry: pH 7 is neutral, and pH 1, with the 1 as I, is extremely acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet comes from Greece, a country of the Balkan peninsula.

clue.text: Top tennis sites where there's likely to be action

definitions.text: where there's likely to be action

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head or of a hill
tennis is played on courts

explanation.surface: The best tennis venues are where the exciting play is likely to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' means a lawsuit; Crown Courts are where serious criminal cases are tried in England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a case brought before a court, and these English courts hear criminal trials.

clue.text: Imperial measure that most anglers use

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length, five and a half yards, also called a pole or perch
the long flexible pole fishermen cast with

explanation.surface: A traditional measurement that most fishermen rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both an old British length unit and the fishing pole anglers hold.

clue.text: Privacy I lost, due to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their private life vanished because of reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' sounds like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'reform' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone and undisturbed by others is the state of seclusion that privacy describes.

clue.text: Following shot, retreat's ordered

indicators.note: the retreat comes following the word for shot

parts.note: a shot at something is an attempt or bid
a den is a private retreat or study

explanation.surface: After a gunshot, a retreat is ordered by the commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' and 'retreat' read as military; they are an attempt and a private room.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidden is the old past participle of bid, meaning commanded or told to do something.
